title: Photo era
about: Date a photo from its look alone: grain, colour, sharpness, framing. Pictures come from the Wikipedia decade articles; when the file has a date you need the exact year, otherwise anything in the decade counts.

decades.look: Black & white glass plates, very sharp in daylight, stiff poses, ghostly blur on moving people
Black & white or sepia; WW1 press photos; first autochromes (soft, grainy, pastel colour)
Black & white, softer press photos, more amateur snapshots (Kodak Brownie)
Sharper 35 mm street shots (Leica); Kodachrome colour slides from 1936
Mostly black & white war photography; rare, very saturated Kodachrome
Black & white press photos; saturated Kodachrome/Ektachrome in travel shots and ads
Colour snapshots spread; square prints with white borders; B&W still common in the press
Warm, faded orange/yellow colour cast, soft grain, muted greens
Bright on-camera flash, red-eye, saturated colour film, orange date stamps
Clean colour film, disposable cameras, date stamps; first digital cameras late in the decade
Early digital: low resolution, blown-out skies, purple fringing, noisy night shots
Sharp HDR phone photos, wide-angle, portrait-mode blur, Instagram filters
